blueprint_inputs.why: Counting stats and advanced metrics voters see.
Who votes, how many ballot slots and when ballots are cast determine which information can matter.
Team success correlates with winning.
Goalie awards depend on save percentage and workload.
Narrative around rookies and age curves influence voters for Calder and comeback-style awards.
Games played and late injuries.
Late narrative events (injury, milestone, scandal) can swing voters, especially before ballot deadlines.
Finalist announcements and the award date define when information resolves and when markets can close.

unreg:draft_selection.blueprint_mechanism: Award outcomes are a mixture of measurable production and voter narrative, filtered through ballot structure and timing; the best predictor is a voter-behaviour model fit on historical finalists with stats, team success and position. Late-season injuries and finalist announcements are discrete information events.
unreg:draft_selection.label: NHL draft selections (top pick and draft slot)

live_series.reviewer_reason: Pro Hockey Draft Pick: no markets listed and no rules text; title suggests which player or team is picked at a draft slot. Outcome is a league draft decision (lottery order, team needs, prospect ranking), which fits no award or standings archetype. Settlement unverified.
live_series.title: Pro Hockey Draft Pick

live_series.reviewer_reason: Pro Hockey Top Pick: no markets listed and no rules text; title suggests who is selected first overall. Outcome is a league draft decision (lottery order, team needs, prospect ranking), which fits no award or standings archetype. Settlement unverified.
live_series.title: Pro Hockey Top Pick

unreg:draft_selection.target: Which player or team is selected at a given draft position, determined by the league's lottery and team decisions.
unreg:draft_selection.why_distinct: Outcome is generated by lottery odds, team draft-order ownership and club selection choices over a prospect board, not by on-ice performance, voting for awards, or standings races.

blueprint_inputs.why: Calibrated team strength with uncertainty.
Process-based offence component of ratings.
Process-based defence component.
Goalie is the largest single-player driver, especially in playoffs.
Long-term injuries to stars change strength.
Remaining schedule difficulty and games in hand.
Qualification and seeding in tight races are decided by formal tie-break order, not raw points.
Series state for playoff series markets.
Lucky shooting/save runs inflate standings; regress before simulating the rest of the season.
Playoff-specific TOI and penalty environment.
Trades, coaching changes and signings shift team strength after public ratings were fitted.
Sportsbook futures prices are a benchmark for rating-based probabilities and show the market's information.

unreg:playoff_series_aggregate.blueprint_mechanism: These markets integrate team strength over many games or a short series: probability is the result of a simulation using team ratings with their uncertainty, injuries, schedule, tiebreakers and bracket structure. Futures are heavily influenced by rating uncertainty and by information that arrives slowly (injuries, trades), and hold time of capital matters.
unreg:playoff_series_aggregate.label: NHL playoff series aggregate outcomes (series total goals and related series-length props)

live_series.reviewer_reason: Title 'NHL Series Total Goals', no markets or rules. The outcome is total goals summed over a random-length 4-7 game playoff series. Series length depends on how evenly matched the teams are (close matchups mean more games and more goals). Neither the single-game total archetype nor season_futures (who wins the series) produces this variable. The strike, OT inclusion and source of truth are unverified.
live_series.title: NHL Series Total Goals

unreg:playoff_series_aggregate.target: A quantity added up across one best-of-7 playoff series (e.g. total goals in all games) compared with a threshold. Its value depends jointly on the number of games played (4-7) and on scoring in each game.
unreg:playoff_series_aggregate.why_distinct: The outcome is a sum over a random number of games, and that number depends on the two teams' per-game win probabilities and the home-ice sequence. The single-game total archetype models one game of fixed length. season_futures models only who wins the series. Ledger siblings on the same mechanism (Series Total Games, Series Game Spread, Series Exact Score, Series Overtime, KXNHLSERIESTOTALGOALS) have no listed markets and are not in this pack.
